newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldovan discount rate falls to 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Moldovan discount rate falls to 20 pct.

text.p: Moldova's National Bank cut its discount rate to 20 percent on Wednesday from the 22 percent in force since September 4, the bank said on Thursday.
The new rate was set at a credit auction where 17 banks acquired 28.32 million lei ($6.11 million) of National Bank's reserves.
The credit funds were allotted to the banks for refinancing purposes for three months.
In line with agreements with the International Monetary Fund, the National Bank has eliminated cheap loans and channels over 80 percent of its credits to the economy only through regular auctions.
Official discount rates have been falling from a high of 377 percent in February 1994, as the former Soviet republic stamped out hyperinflation.
The authorities expect annual inflation to fall this year to 17 percent from 23.8 percent in 1995.
